hints: Notice the wiring of the two identical speakers in series - the same a.c. current drives both cones in the same direction at the same time, so the two sound waves start in phase.

Think about path difference along PQ: at the midpoint the distances are equal for constructive interference, and moving toward P or Q changes the path difference by multiples of $\lambda/2$ to give alternate loud and quiet points.

Compare the distances to the two speakers at the centre and near P or Q - where are the two amplitudes most equal so cancellation is most complete, and where is the microphone closest overall so the maxima are largest.
walkthrough: The series connection drives the identical speakers with the same current in the same sense, so their cones vibrate in step. The two sound sources are coherent and in phase with phase difference $0$.

For a microphone position on PQ, the interference depends on path difference $\Delta = |r_1 - r_2|$. At the midpoint $r_1 = r_2$, so $\Delta = 0$ gives constructive interference and an intensity maximum at the centre.

Moving along PQ changes $\Delta$. When $\Delta = n\lambda$ there is constructive interference and a loud maximum; when $\Delta = (n+1/2)\lambda$ there is destructive interference and a quiet minimum. This gives several maxima and minima between P and Q.

Intensity depends on resultant amplitude, with $I \propto A^2$. The wave amplitude from each speaker falls with distance. Near the centre the microphone is closest overall, so the maxima are tallest there and fall off toward P and Q.

Cancellation can be complete only if the two amplitudes are equal. This is most nearly true near the centre where $r_1 \approx r_2$, so minima are deepest near the centre and rise above zero toward P and Q where one speaker dominates. Minima therefore do not all reach zero.
That combination - central maximum, modulated envelope largest in the middle, and minima that are lowest near the centre but generally non-zero - matches the shape shown. This is option A.

A.explanation: Shows alternating maxima and non-zero minima with largest envelope and deepest minima near the centre, as expected for two in-phase sources at different distances.

B.explanation: Shows minima reaching zero at all positions, which would need equal amplitudes from the two speakers at every point on PQ.

C.explanation: Shows constant maximum height and constant minimum height, which ignores the fall of amplitude with distance from the speakers.

D.explanation: Shows constant envelope with zero minima everywhere, which ignores both unequal amplitudes off-centre and greater closeness at the centre.
